body:
Replaces #108, closed when `--delete-branch` removed its base on the #106 merge. Same head branch, same commits, retargeted to master.

Two commits: the lane's store, then the integration reconciliation the lane was deliberately not allowed to make.

## The store

Transcribed from the registry's §11 declaration, not designed. Six packed columns at `CAPACITY = 64` in declared ordinal order, plus the two declared scalars. Allocated once in `_init()`; `resize()` appears only in `_allocate_columns()`. `_assert_contracts()` proves the eight keys, ordinals, type codes and SAVE-R09-005's 32-byte stride at construction, so a renumbering edit fails at `_init()` rather than at a save.

Allocate-before-consume (ADR 0059): `_advance_sequence()` is the last statement of `schedule_into()`, so a full / exhausted / non-int32 / non-future refusal leaves the store byte-identical including `_next_sequence`. Day boundaries only via `(tick + 4500) mod 18000` — never `tick % 18000`, which is 06:00.

Ten mutations, all died, one per Godot invocation with a `shasum -a 256` byte-compare between runs.

## The reconciliation

`WorldRuntime.next_event_sequence` moves to EventSchedule ownership: **8 bytes changing owner, not 8 added.** WorldRuntime's I64 row drops 3 columns → 2 (24 → 16), EventSchedule gains a 1-column row (8). Net zero; every ledger total unchanged.

`packed_source_field_count` 530 → **536**. `record_count` stays **582** — §11's eight fields were declared long before a module implemented them.

## Three things the lane got wrong

All from computing against a base that moved underneath it:

| Reported | Actual |
|---|---|
| Ledger at lines 417/418/425 | The injury repair moved them to **434/435/441** |
| Next contract key `C168` | C168–C170 already taken → **C171** |
| `3943 test(s), 0 failure(s)` | On the rebased tree: `4043 test(s), **1 failure**` |

That failure was `test_registry_counts_are_the_ones_the_ruling_reconciled`, pinning `REGISTRY_PACKED_FIELD_COUNT = 530`. The pin now carries its reason — REG-R01 *requires* it to grow, while `record_count` must not move without a ruling.

## Evidence

```
./tools/run_tests.sh
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 51 modules, 335 rows, 654 packed columns checked
4043 test(s), 139176 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

`ready07_arithmetic` PASS · `merge_gate` PASS · `decision_numbers` PASS · `validate_save_registry_handoff --source-root .` PASS (536 packed fields, 50 owners, 582 records).

DEVIATIONS: none
SURVIVED_MUTANTS: none
BLOCKED: none

## Scope deliberately not claimed

§11 has **no codec** — nothing encodes or decodes `next_sequence:i64` + N 32-byte records — and **no ruled kind/argument domain**, so `_kind`/`_source_id`/`_arg0`/`_arg1` are validated as int32 storage carrying no meaning. There is no producer, no consumer, and the store is wired into no autoload. No release-save completeness is claimed and §15's digest is not unblocked by this alone.

Neither is a defect in this change, and neither makes it unsafe to merge — this store is additive and nothing depends on it yet. Stating it under `BLOCKED:` previously held the PR, which conflated "unsafe to merge" with "scope not claimed"; that field now means only the former.

body:
Replaces #107, which GitHub closed when `--delete-branch` removed its base branch on the #106 merge. Same head branch, same commits, retargeted to master. That auto-close is a real bug in `tools/auto_merge.py` and is fixed in a follow-up.

Answers "build this whole process — fully automated end to end, with approval for art" and "a prompt to give Astra so it can build its own loop".

Contract: [`docs/automation/README.md`](docs/automation/README.md). Recorded as [ADR 0129](docs/decisions/0129-the-development-loop-stops-only-for-art.md).

## The cycle

`work_queue.json` → `dispatch_plan.py` → subagents with file allowlists → PR from the template → CI → `auto_merge.py` → merged → dependants unblock → repeat. Two side channels feed the same queue: `OPEN.md` for questions only Astra can answer, `art_approvals.json` for things only Brendan can.

| Tool | Refuses |
|---|---|
| `dispatch_plan.py` | Tasks whose owned paths intersect each other or anything `in_flight` **or `review`**. `--validate` also refuses cycles, unknown deps, and art gates with no approval id. |
| `auto_merge.py` | Any PR failing one of four: all checks SUCCESS (not pending), mergeable and not draft, `merge_gate.py` against the **branch's** ledger, all three declarations present and empty. |
| `art_gate.py` | Anything not `approved` by a named human. No `--force`, no env var, no agent-writable path. |
| `astra_inbox.py --check` | A stale `OPEN.md`. |

## Why art is the only stop

Paid generation spends Brendan's money and reverting a commit does not refund it. Visual acceptance is taste — no test asserts whether the badger reads as a badger, and an agent accepting its own art is grading its own work. Decision 0002 separately forbids bulk creature generation before proportion approval.

The `DEVIATIONS`/`SURVIVED_MUTANTS`/`BLOCKED` blocks keep a human in the loop without keeping them in the way: most changes declare nothing and merge untouched. A lane once overruled my brief **correctly**, citing SAVE-LAYOUT-R01 over the instruction I gave it — a script that ranked that would be wrong whichever way it ruled, so it stops and surfaces instead.

## Proven in use since it was written

Five lanes ran through it. It caught a stale test pin, a contract-key collision, three stale ledger citations, and — on PR #112 — **six false positives from its own L2 check**, which is now scoped to one owner with the failing fixture kept as a regression case.

## Bug found while building it

`gh api -f ref=<branch>` sends a **request body**, which a GET ignores — so the ledger fetch silently returned the default branch's file. `auto_merge.py` would have checked master's ledger and called it the PR's. Fixed to a query string, with the reason written beside it.

DEVIATIONS: none
SURVIVED_MUTANTS: none
BLOCKED: none

body:
Stacked on #111 → #110 → #109 → #108 → #106. REQ-SET-124–128/137's project lifecycle as its own store — **not** a second Building store. The Building state machine (BLUEPRINT → BUILDING → ACTIVE, ACTIVE → DEMOLISHING → gone) is driven from here.

Delivery before work; consumption at exactly **one** transition (`begin_work()`); 100%-before / 80%-after cancellation refund floored to milli-U; evacuation before demolition; demolition priced at declared construction WU × 0.25 returning 50% of the original §4.1 cost. Two-phase cancellation and completion, both idempotent on retry, so a failed output publishes nothing.

The 100%/80% and 50% paths **refuse each other** — ARCH-JOB-004's ban on a shared "refund all" helper is structural here, not a comment. `_work_begun` is its own column because it is not derivable from `_remaining_mwu`: a project with full remaining work has not necessarily begun.

## This PR proved my own merge gate wrong

L2 refused it with **six false positives** — `present`, `ref_slot`, `ref_generation`, `type_id`, `phase`, `purpose` — colliding ConstructionIndex against BuildingIndex, FurnitureIndex and RoomIndex. Not one shares a byte.

L2 flags a field written `x` in one row and `_x` in another, on the theory it is one byte budgeted twice. **That holds only within one owner**, which is what the real Injury defect was. §3's index tables name members bare while a store's own section spells them as GDScript does.

Fixed both ways: L2 now compares only rows whose owner labels share a leading token, `test_merge_gate.py` gained the exact false-positive fixture as a regression case, and these rows switched to bare names to match the §3 convention they'd broken.

## Ledger

Three §3 rows, **5,142,528 bytes**. The lane computed its figures against `origin/master`, so all seven identities were wrong for this tree:

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Payload | 66968467 | **72110995** |
| Live world | 75357075 | **80499603** |
| Transactional peak | 136109958 | **146395014** |

Live keeps 19,500,397 bytes of headroom. §2.2's existing Construction columns are not re-added or enlarged; the bill tables are 3828 bytes inside §2.3's existing arena and owe no row.

## Mutations: 13, two declared survivors, neither waved through

The five named in the brief all die: M9/M1 (refusal that still consumed / still published), M2+M3 (the 100%/80% boundary — both the fraction *and* its placement), M4 (demolition fraction), M5+M7 (work before delivery), M6 (cancelled construction leaving a live row).

**M12 is unreachable, not untested.** `_refund_policy` is written only by `_policy_for()`, the same function the check runs, so no public call sequence can disagree; its caller is the save decoder, which does not exist. ADR 0088 records the identical caveat for `buildings.verify_room_masks()`.

**M13 is equivalent.** PHASE_READY is reachable today only through complete delivery. The gate is deliberate defence against a decoder writing PHASE_READY over an empty ledger — which is exactly what M7's 30 kills show matters. It was not deleted to manufacture a kill.

**Harness incident, disclosed by the lane and recorded in ADR 0131:** a second harness was launched before the first finished; both mutated the same file, producing one false `MUTATION_NOT_APPLIED` and one inflated kill count. Every contaminated verdict was discarded, the harness took a single-instance lock, and all 13 were re-run from a restored file, reproducing the earlier clean run mutation for mutation.

## What is NOT done

**06.1 is left unchecked and the starter settlement is still empty** — 0 buildings, 0 rooms, 0 furniture, 0 projects, now pinned by a test rather than assumed. No Job and no tick stage: `TICK_STAGE_COUNT` is still **8** and that test is unchanged; nothing calls `add_work_mwu()` yet. The dispatcher integration (PLACE_BLUEPRINT, DEMOLISH, …) is not started.

```
./tools/run_tests.sh
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 52 modules, 350 rows, 681 packed columns checked
4238 test(s), 142421 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

DEVIATIONS: none
SURVIVED_MUTANTS: M12 unreachable, M13 equivalent — both argued above, neither deleted to manufacture a kill
BLOCKED: none

### Scope not claimed (not merge-blockers)

REQ-SET-128's stored-goods half needs container-by-owner enumeration from `inventory.gd`; the tier-2 demolition basis is unresolved and uses the base §4.1 row at every tier; 06.1 is left unchecked and the starter settlement is still empty. All three are filed in Astra's inbox. None makes this change unsafe to merge — it is additive and nothing depends on it yet.

Merged on Brendan's explicit instruction with the two declared survivors standing: M12 unreachable, M13 equivalent, both argued above.

body:
Stacked on #110 → #109 → #108 → #106. **This is the dependency that was holding all twelve section codecs.** Every one could encode; none could capture from or restore into a live store. Decision 0105 solved it for `entity_directory.gd`; this extends the pattern to the three largest §4 COMPONENT_COLUMNS owners.

`needs.gd` (20 columns), `residents.gd` (19), `jobs.gd` (38 §4 + 4 §5, restored as one transaction). Each publishes `copy_columns_into()`, `restore_columns()`, `last_column_refusal()`, `state_bytes()` and its declared ordinal tables.

`docs/persistence_state_registry.md` and `canonical_state_registry.json` **agree for all three modules** — nothing needed adjudication. The suites re-read the JSON artifact and compare ordinal by ordinal.

## One deliberate departure from 0105

The directory takes six positional buffers. Twenty, nineteen and forty-two do not fit that shape, so the buffers travel in a per-store `Columns` inner class — allocated once to declared extents, one named public field per category-1 column in ordinal order, caller-owned and refilled in place exactly as 0105 requires. Re-verified on 4.7.2 that packed arrays are true references through a class member as well as a local *before* anything was written against the assumption.

## Restore ordering is now enforced, not documented

1. §3 before `residents.gd`; §3 **and** `residents.gd` before `jobs.gd`. A reference the directory does not honour refuses; a JobAgent row on an absent resident refuses.
2. §14 must run after §4 for names. `restore_columns()` installs `_named` and empties every `_name_key`; `unresolved_name_row_count()` returns a count, never a sentinel.
3. `jobs.gd`'s §4 and §5 restore as **one call** — a half-applied pair is not a state the store can hold.

## Five mutants survived, and none were waved through

Three were checks no input could reach, **deleted** with the reasoning written into the docstrings: the worker-binding `named != bound_jobs` comparison; an `agent_present != 1` guard the free-agent-row rule already subsumes; and the generation half of the job→agent reference comparison.

Two were **missing coverage**, and got tests: deleting the *slot* half of that comparison survived until "two live jobs claiming one worker" was added, deliberately on the same directory generation so nothing else separates them; and widening the *negative* need-remainder bound survived a positive-only boundary test — decay leaves negative remainders, so that was the side that mattered.

32 runs over 26 sites, one mutation per Godot invocation, each file `shasum -a 256` byte-compared after every restore. The member-chain step-cap mutant kills by **non-termination**, blowing the harness alarm with no summary line — which is what `test_a_cyclic_member_chain_refuses_instead_of_hanging` is named for, and is recorded as a hang rather than a failure count.

## An environment finding, proved rather than assumed

On the fresh worktree *before* `--editor --quit`, the suite reported `3912 test(s), 36 failure(s)` — and reported the **identical 36-failure set with all three production files reverted to `origin/master`**. All were UI/theme/font suites on unimported resources. That is how you establish "not mine".

## Corrected a stale production comment

`residents.gd`'s header asserted there was no restore writer because inventing one would invent migration provenance. The store half now exists and infers nothing — `_life_stage` arrives in the column set or the call refuses, and no row is repaired to ADULT. Refusing a **pre-column schema** remains the codec's job through `owner_schema_version`, because a store handed a column set cannot see which schema produced it.

## Rebase note

Conflicted on `docs/tasks/09_persistence_replay_reliability.md` — two lanes each appending a dated section. Mechanical keep-both; both survive at lines 501 and 604.

**No ledger byte owed.** Everything published is a reader, validator, refusal code or inner class. Three existing category-3 scratch rows extended for `_last_column_refusal` rather than three new rows added.

```
./tools/run_tests.sh
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 51 modules, 335 rows, 654 packed columns checked
4188 test(s), 141922 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

No release-save completeness claimed: there is still no §4 COMPONENT_COLUMNS codec and no §5 CHILD_ARENAS codec. These are the store halves only. BLOCKER J2 is untouched — it names `job_planner.gd`, a different module.

SURVIVED_MUTANTS: none
BLOCKED: none

Stacked on #109 → #108 → #106. Implements ALERT-R02: NARROW always compact; STANDARD/WIDE prefer the complete text with adaptive fitting and fallback inside the existing zone.

The second alert card is a second **instance** of UI-SET-011, not a new §4 id — §4 catalogues one "Alert card" row and §8.2 lists 011 once. It shares the registry row, hit-test id and accessible role, carries node suffix `alert_card_2`, and its tab stop is spliced at the `Control` level because `ui_focus_order.gd` is keyed on §4 ids and is not this lane's file.

`alert_stack_into` gained an explicit `count`: the shell's measured buffer is preallocated at 2, so `measured.size()` could not express "how many notices want a card" and the second slot rendered as an empty card. Out-of-range refuses with `UI_INVALID_ALERT_NOTICE_COUNT`.

A card prints *exactly* `notice.summary` or *exactly* `notice.message` — no third truncating branch. The accessible description carries the whole message either way.

## Two things measured that the ruling could not have known

Neither was fixed here. Both are premises, and correcting a premise is not an implementation choice — they are now items in Astra's inbox.

**1. The 44px full card is unreachable typography.** ALERT-R02 states two 44px full cards fit exactly in the 92px zone. In the real theme one wrapped line is **23px**, and §1.2's padding is 12px top and bottom, so the smallest possible *full* card is **47px**. A 47px first card leaves 41px — under the 44px minimum — and the second notice is not placed. Captures `36`/`37` show one card where the ruling implies two; `32`/`33`, where card one is a 44px *summary*, show two. The rail states it correctly in both.

**2. §1.2 publishes two rectangles that collide at the supported floor.** At 1280×720 @100% the alert zone `(460, 16, 360, 96)` lies **wholly inside** the workspace/modal frame `(160, 16, 960, 688)`. Same at @150%. At 1920×1080 the frame starts at y=180 and there is no overlap. This is **not** a z-order bug: §3's layer table puts workspace at layer 40 and permanent HUD zones at layer 20, so the workspace drawing over the alert zone is the specification working as written. Both cards are placed correctly and report `visible = true`. Captured as evidence `40`; recorded open in ADR 0134 and the task checklist.

## Evidence

`docs/validation/evidence/ui-refinement/screenshots/`, files `32`–`40`, native macOS, windowed, absolute `save_png` path. The harness supplies **no message text**: the Info line is `main.gd`'s own boot alert and the Error line comes from choosing HOLT in UI-SET-103 and running the real `create_world()`.

Nothing overflows or clips in any capture. Pre-existing and not this lane's: counter cells clip (ADR 0076) and the NARROW command strip overlaps the minimap frame.

Ten mutations, all killed, one Godot invocation each with a `shasum -a 256` byte-compare between runs. M4a/M4b split the required "stack exceeding its zone" mutant so each run mutates one line.

**No new packed column, so no ledger or registry row is owed.**

```
./tools/run_tests.sh
state_registry_coverage: PASS -- 51 modules, 335 rows, 654 packed columns checked
4109 test(s), 141364 assertion(s), 0 failure(s)
```

The lane's own `3931 / 0` was measured before the rebase; this is the post-rebase number.

ART-UI-12's visual verdict stays open. No visual approval and no screen-reader qualification are claimed — both cards' names and descriptions are set and asserted, but no assistive technology was run.

Stacked on #108 → #106. **Residents render for the first time.** `World/Entities` was empty and nothing consumed `presentation_extract.gd`; now twelve mice draw from a `MultiMeshInstance3D` with 512 instances preallocated in `_init()` and `visible_instance_count` following the living.

Fifteen mutations, all killed, one Godot invocation each with a `shasum -a 256` byte-compare between runs. Two of them — M5 (`is_present` instead of `is_alive`, so the dead keep drawing) and M7 (the filled buffer never reaches the MultiMesh) — were added *after* writing the tests that catch them; the original suite let both through, because despawn clears presence and life together and every other test read the private buffer rather than the MultiMesh.

## What you can see, and what is wrong with it

Untextured white, bind pose with arms out, standing in a rigid straight line. The straight line is not a rendering bug — see below.

The lane predicted the mice would face backwards. **They don't** — the closeup shows them facing the camera. Correcting that here so nobody chases it.

Pre-existing and not this lane's: the HUD still reads `Residents --` and `No world generated` after a successful generation, visible in the before capture too.

## The line is a refusal, not a layout

**No resident in the running game has an authoritative position.** `settlement_system.gd` composes fourteen core stores and `transforms.gd` is not one of them, so nothing calls `place()`. And GDD §5.1 authors no spawn coordinates — only that room assignments follow resident ID ascending and bed ID ascending, and beds need a Furniture store `world_init.gd`'s own header records as BLOCKED.

Writing an invented layout into authoritative state is the invented production constant the movement amendment forbids, so the lane built a presentation-private pose store instead: read by no tick stage, in no save section, all geometry derived from `world_init.gd`. The single unauthored choice — which cleared tile a resident stands on — is isolated in `muster_tile_x/z()`.

It costs **3,151,872 bytes**, 98% of this PR's whole ledger delta, and the row is marked *deleted whole* when movement composes ARCH-SYS-001. Now a blocking question for Astra rather than a commit-message footnote.

## Ledger

| Row | Count | Per | Bytes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Resident crowd instance buffer | 512 | 100 | 51200 |
| Presentation pose scaffold Transform store | 87552 | 36 | 3151872 |

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Payload | 63765395 | **66968467** |
| Live world | 72154003 | **75357075** |
| Transactional peak | 129703814 | **136109958** |

Live keeps 24,642,925 bytes of headroom. The peak was already past the gate — that is why ARCH-MEM-006 selected disk-backed rollback.

`docs/validation/evidence/resident-render-path/` — native macOS, windowed, absolute `save_png` paths, plus the before capture at `914444b` showing empty ground. Instance origins `(117.0, 0.5, 139.0)`, `(119.0, …)`, `(121.0, …)`, hand-checkable against §5.9's hall origin and §5.1's tile pitch: `(2048*58+1024)/1024 = 117.0`.

Answers "can you build something that reviews and catches those merge issues to allow us to automate the merge as well".

`docs/validation/merge_gate.py` runs four checks in the `contracts` job — no engine, no LFS, under a second. Every one is a defect that actually reached a PR here, passed the full Godot suite and every other validator, and was caught only by a human recomputing the arithmetic.

| Check | Refuses |
|---|---|
| **L1** | A trail row whose running payload is not the row above plus its own delta, or whose reserve column is not payload + 8388608. Checked row by row: comparing totals is what let five merges through. |
| **L2** | A field written `x` in one ledger row and `_x` in another — one byte budgeted twice, once under the planned component and once under the store implementing it. |
| **L3** | A ledger row where width × columns × rows ≠ its own byte total. |
| **A1** | An agent report whose `DEVIATIONS:` / `SURVIVED_MUTANTS:` / `BLOCKED:` blocks are non-empty **or missing**. |

A1 does not judge the exception — a lane that overrules its brief may be right, and one was, citing SAVE-LAYOUT-R01 over my instruction. It removes the change from the automatic path so a human reads it.

## L2 fired on its author's own change

Decision 0109 added all eleven of `injury.gd`'s columns to §3 as **+21504**, while §2.2 already carried the Injury component's rows budgeting `kind`, `severity`, `rescuer_slot`, `rescuer_generation` and `care_progress_mwu` at 10240 + 4096. **14336 bytes counted twice.**

The repair moves `injury.gd`'s actual layout into §2.2 — where implemented component columns live, as `residents.gd`'s own `_named`/`_selected` are — and reduces 0109's trail delta to its net **+7168**:

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| §2.2 | 142 rows / 25029474 | **144 rows / 25036642** |
| §3 | — | **72 rows / 20150752** |
| Payload | 63779731 | **63765395** |
| Live world | 72168339 | **72154003** |
| Transactional peak | 129732486 | **129703814** |

`ready07_arithmetic.py`'s `DECISION_0109_ADDED` now carries the subtraction with the reason beside it.

## The negative case is a first-class test

A gate that only ever passes is indistinguishable from a gate that does nothing. `test_merge_gate.py` drives all four checks with the defect they exist for *and* with a clean input — eleven cases, including the reduced form of this double budget and the bare-name case (`Building`, `FarmPlot`, `Feast`, `Job` and `RngStream` each legitimately carry their own `state`) that made the discarded first draft emit 84 false positives.

Verified by hand: the gate REFUSES the pre-repair tree with 6 problems and PASSES the repaired one, with `docs/systems_architecture.md` byte-identical by `shasum -a 256` after the experiment.

Recorded as [ADR 0128](docs/decisions/0128-the-merge-gate-and-the-injury-double-budget-it-found.md).

body:
**`ok: 4012 tests, 138867 assertions, 0 failures.`** All four validators PASS. 43 tests, 10 mutations, all killed.

§15 was previously impossible: the digest is *defined over* ordered field records, and the registry supplying that order did not exist until this session.

## The result that matters

Run against the production declaration, `digest_into()` **refuses** with `CANONICAL_NO_ADAPTER` and names **all 50 owners** in walk order. That is the correct behaviour, and it is also the measurement: **zero adapters exist.**

`DigestResult.covers_release_state` is false on every result this branch can produce. There is **no subset mode, no empty-adapter default and no flag that relaxes the coverage gate** — the release/fixture distinction lives in the API, not the docs.

## A fixture anyone can reproduce by hand

Three owners, seven declared fields, six records, **426 bytes**, SHA-256 `7711d6b5dcd94db94f82bb4d61fb976506ffb57aec60eb62d94d4051aad61da0` — pinned as constants computed **independently in Python**, split by stream element.

It is built to discriminate: `"Zed"` < `"alpha"` in ASCII but not case-insensitively or by length; `"Zed"`'s declared ordinals (`_zulu`, `_alpha`) **disagree with alphabetical order**; `alpha._excluded_tick` is `hash=false` and emits nothing; `"Móle"` is 4 characters and 5 UTF-8 bytes.

Mutations confirm each of those is load-bearing: walking alphabetically instead of by declared ordinal dies 6 times; **case-folding the owner comparison** dies 26; walking owners in reverse dies 6; writing a string's **character** count as its u32 length dies 8; emitting the excluded field dies 8.

## Three design decisions with their costs stated

**A compiled table, not a runtime JSON read.** Two deciding facts: `docs/planning/` is outside `res://` so an exported build cannot reach it, and Godot's `JSON.parse_string()` returns every number as a **float**, which would put a float on the ordering path. `test_module_has_no_float_and_no_dictionary()` greps the non-comment source for `float`, `Dictionary` and `JSON.`. Two further tests prove the table matches the JSON, so it cannot be hand-edited.

**The u32 sign trap is handled by making the adapter declare its storage form.** `STORAGE_INT32` reinterprets two's-complement bits (`rng._state`, and `entity_directory._next_persistent_id` whose declared range reaches 2147483648); `STORAGE_INT64` carries a logical value range-checked to `0..4294967295`. **Neither is a default**, and a negative u64 refuses rather than emitting a number GDScript could never have meant.

`inventory`'s **first declared column is the scalar `_c_free_count` with element count 1** — so inferring an extent from it yields neither 101376 nor 16384. `primary_count` is the container capacity, with `_l_capacity` as its one declared child extent in a `child_extent_count:u32` + `u64[]` block. **No category-2 member**: `_free_heap`, `_job_head`, `_lot_head` and the four chain-link columns are rebuilt by their owners, and every count is recomputed from occupancy.

**But it does write** `inventory`'s `_c_free`/`_l_free` and `stock_age`'s `_declared_slots` — because those are stacks and a swap-ordered dense list whose **permutation is observable** — and only `[0, count)`, since the tail is stale garbage two identical worlds can disagree about. **`inventory.gd` does not blank a retired row.** `_retire_lot()` leaves `_l_item_id`, `_l_quality` and `_l_provenance` at their last live values, unlike `fishing`, `forage`, `gear` and `reservations`, which blank completely.

NAME-R02 **corrects SAVE-R09-002**: live anonymous residents are legal. The old reading refused the starter settlement, where eleven of twelve founders are anonymous.

## The fixture that makes the scalar rule real

`Residents.name_refusal()` is the only place the rules exist — reached by `set_name()`, `restore_name()`, automatic Warden assignment, `capture_into()`, `record_refusal()` and `apply()`. The codec adds no rule; it maps the code onto its own vocabulary.

The discriminating fixture is `"A" + U+0301` × 17 — **34 scalars, 51 UTF-8 bytes, 17 grapheme clusters**:

- a **byte** counter sees 51 against a 128-byte cap and **admits** it
- a **grapheme cluster** counter sees 17 against 32 and **admits** it
- only the **scalar** rule refuses

One fixture kills both wrong units. That is the ruling's "do not count bytes or grapheme clusters as scalar length" turned into a test rather than a comment.

Two more judgements worth reading: `utf8_byte_length_of()` is **arithmetic** over the 0x7F/0x7FF/0xFFFF boundaries rather than `to_utf8_buffer().size()`, which keeps `residents.gd` from preloading the codec (the dependency runs the other way) — and it is asserted equal to a real encode on six fixtures. The control test is **three integer bounds**, not an engine category lookup, exactly as ruled.

Engine limits handled honestly: Godot cannot represent U+0000 in a `String` (`String.chr(0)` yields U+FFFD), so NUL is asserted against `is_control_scalar(0x00)` directly while the string-level loop covers `0x09, 0x0A, 0x1F, 0x7F, 0x80, 0x9F`.

## The §14 wrapper, with measured bytes

On the real starter settlement — 11 anonymous founders plus "Warden Rowan" — the section is **2101 bytes**:

```
framing   [0:37]  01000000 09000000 7265736964656e7473 01000000 0002000000000000 1008000000000000
row_count [37:41] 00020000
slot 0    [41:57] 0c000000 57617264656e20526f77616e
slot 1    [57:61] 00000000
```

Canonical contribution **2060**, section **2101** — delta **exactly 41** (4 `store_count` + 33 wrapper + 4 retained `row_count`). `payload_byte_length` is validated against `length - 37` **from the descriptor**, not merely against bounds.

## The ordering rule, which is N4's real content

`occupancy_refusal()` runs over all 512 rows **before `apply()`'s first write**. Writes go through `restore_name(slot, named, name)`, which takes the flag explicitly — §14 restores names, §4 owns the flag. The incoming flag column is snapshotted once before the first write so a rollback restores the exact prior pair.

`test_encode_store_refuses_a_live_name_that_breaks_the_alias_rule` asserted `set_name()` **accepts** a 40-scalar name — blocker N3 stated as a fact. `test_apply_sets_the_named_flag_from_the_key_for_every_row` asserted `apply()` **derives** `_named` from the key — exactly the concealment N4 names. Both replaced with tests of the ruled behaviour, including both mismatch directions and one proving the verdict is available before any write.

Scalar length counted as bytes dies 12 times; an anonymous live row refused dies 14; the owner-key spelling changed dies 20; the wrapper's `payload_byte_length` disagreeing with the body dies 11.

**An honest caveat on M9**, stated by the lane rather than glossed: it is a two-line mutation run alone, and the `restore_name → set_name` swap *by itself* is an equivalent mutant once the precondition is intact. It did not claim a separate kill for it.

The canonical artifact **already declared** primary_count 512, max_payload_bytes 67588, max_section_bytes 67625 and `section_schema_versions[13] = 2` — verified, and the lane checked its constants against the artifact rather than deriving them from it. What was stale is `wire.format`, which described the inner payload only; it now names `store_count`, the wrapper and the retained `row_count`, with `framing_bytes 37`.

`persistence_state_registry.md`'s two §14 rows carried pre-wrapper framing and payload-only arithmetic; both updated, plus the 512-byte `_named` snapshot declared as a cold-path transient. **No packed column added, so no ledger byte moves.**

`command_dispatch.gd::_alias_refusal()` is still a **second copy** of the name rules, and its control test misses **C1 U+0080–U+009F**. Those surface as `RESULT_STORE_REFUSED` instead of `RESULT_ALIAS_CONTROL_CHARACTER` — a *reporting* gap only; no invalid name reaches a column either way. Folding it into `Residents.name_refusal()` belongs to that file's owner.

**Not claimed:** §4 has no codec, so nothing restores `_named` yet — `apply()`'s cross-check is only as meaningful as the flags the caller installed. The load orchestrator holding §4-then-§14 is still owed. §15, the canonical field walker and cross-process parity are untouched.

## The defect, confirmed before fixing — and confirmed the right way

`ui_manager.gd` held `_roster_slots: PackedInt32Array` — bare slots — and guarded a click with `residents.is_alive(slot)`.

`entity_directory.create()` pops the **lowest free directory slot and the lowest free typed row**, so a despawn immediately followed by a spawn returns the same resident row at generation + 1. `is_alive(slot)` is true again, and the old row opened the detail panel **on the replacement**.

The lane didn't assert this — it ran its six new tests against `git show HEAD:…/ui_manager.gd` and got **5 of 6 failing**. The sixth is the "refreshed row still works" half, which correctly passes both ways. That is the right way to prove a test catches the thing it claims to.

## What landed

Three packed int32 columns plus a scalar count, resized once in **`_init()` and not `_ready()`** — the suite builds this router off-tree, so a tree-time allocation would be empty there.

A click runs `_roster_identity_refusal()` **first**: `is_valid_of_kind(ref, KIND_RESIDENT)`, then cached persistent id against `get_persistent_id(ref)`; only then is the typed row resolved.

**Three distinct codes rather than one word for three conditions** — `UI_ROSTER_ROW_IS_STALE` (slot empty), `UI_ROSTER_SLOT_REUSED` (slot live, different entity), `UI_ROSTER_IDENTITY_CHANGED` (valid ref, different persistent id). A player being told "that resident is gone" and "that row now points at someone else" are different facts.

`_show_resident_detail()` now takes the validated ref *and* the resolved row and fills needs through `fill_needs_for(...)`. Switching that call alone would have been cosmetic, which is why the storage went first.

## Mutations: 5 killed, 1 honestly equivalent

All four the brief required to die, died — the generation dropped, `is_alive()` restored as the only guard, the persistent-id comparison deleted, and a stale row selecting the replacement instead of refusing (4 failures).

**M6 is reported rather than hidden.** Re-deriving the ref inside `_show_resident_detail()` is a genuine equivalent mutant: that function is only reachable after validation, its `slot` came from `slot_of_ref(ref)`, and `ref_of(slot)` reads back the same pair the reference resolved through. No reachable state distinguishes them. The parameter is kept anyway.

## Ledger: a full +144, not the reported net +96

The lane reported "net +96 against the `_roster_slots` array it replaces." **That assumed the old array was counted, and it was not** — `systems_architecture.md` mentions roster rows only in ARCH-UI-001's prose and has no allocation row for it. Removing it frees no counted byte, so the addition is the full **144** (3 columns × 4 bytes × `ROSTER_POOL` 12). Checked against the document rather than accepted from the report.

Payload **63761203 → 63761347**, peak → **129695718**, allocation rows 27 → 28. **Verified row by row across all 31 trail rows.**

Recorded in the row: `state_registry_coverage.py` globs `godot/scripts/core` only, so it never inspected `ui_manager.gd` and passed identically before and after. A checker-scope gap, not an exemption — which is exactly why the ledger row exists.

Captured from the **native game** at 1280×720 and 150%. The running game printed: `valid` → identity `mouse - Resident - Active`, no refusal; `reused` → identity label **empty**, the panel never opened, `last_refusal()` = `UI_ROSTER_SLOT_REUSED`, roster row still reading `Unnamed resident  mouse`. **The badger that took the slot appears nowhere on screen.**

**The refusal notice is occluded while the roster workspace page is open** — at 1280×720 the workspace panel covers the top-centre alert zone. Stacked on #95, which commits the supplied validator and repairs the contract references it caught.

## The domain

`ORDINARY=0, STARTER=1, COASTAL_BRINE=2, EXCAVATION=3, BACKFILL_RECLAIM=4, SPOIL_RECLAIM=5` — **protected**, not compiled. No `COUNT`, no seventh key.

**All six disagree with ascending ASCII** (`BACKFILL_RECLAIM=0 … STARTER=5`). Unlike `InjuryKind`, where `CUT=1` coincided and made a silent regeneration look half-right, here there is no coincidence at all: a sort would read **every ordinary lot as reclaimed backfill**.

`UNSET_PROVENANCE` keeps the value 0 and is redefined as the compatibility spelling of ORDINARY — `const UNSET_PROVENANCE: int = CatalogScript.PROVENANCE_ORDINARY` — not a seventh member and not an unknown wildcard.

`inventory.gd` refuses a non-member at `create_lot()` with a **new** `REFUSE_INVALID_PROVENANCE`, deliberately distinct from `REFUSE_OVERFLOW` because `6` and `-1` fit an int32 perfectly.

## A boundary worth reading before assuming a gap

**The item-label half is not enforced inside `inventory.gd`.** That store holds an item's compiled id, mass and category and has **never known a key** — `register_item()` takes no name. An id-based second copy of the rule could disagree with the catalog's copy, so the semantic rules live on `catalog.gd` (`check_lot_provenance`, `check_salt_brine_input`, `recipe_output_provenance`, `check_earth_withdrawal`) and the producers that hold the key must call them.

That is a deliberate architectural choice, documented in the docstring and the ADR — not an omission.

## Mutations: 14, all killed

Sorting the domain dies **37** times. Adding `UNSET_PROVENANCE` as a seventh member dies **39**. `_attributes_match()` ignoring provenance dies **43** — merging still requires identical attributes including provenance. Dropping the domain from `PROTECTED_ENUM_DOMAINS` dies 39 plus 6 script errors.

Also killed: salt admitted from non-coastal brine; an earth label without `excavated_earth`; transfer, split and journal rollback dropping provenance; `check_earth_withdrawal()` ignoring the ledger balance; spoilage erasing origin.

Decision 0108's digest-accounting test was **re-pointed at the artifact it replaced** rather than the current one, so 0113's six rows cannot be absorbed into 0108's increment.

## Ledger: no byte moves, but the declaration changes

No new packed column. What changes is **semantics and extent**, which REG-R01 requires declaring: the canonical record `(7, inventory, _l_provenance)` gains `value_domain` and `value_extent: 0..5 inclusive`, so bounded validation is satisfiable **from the declaration** rather than by reading the catalog at runtime.

The state registry row records that an out-of-set value is **refused at load, never clamped**. The `InventoryLot` ledger row keeps every number and gains the §4.3 citation, because §4.3 now numbers provenance and §4.2's closing paragraph no longer reaches it.

## Four things reported, not silently worked around

1. **Saltpan recipe input filter** must call `Catalog.check_salt_brine_input()` — no recipe file was in the allowlist, and no second id-based copy of the rule was added.
2. **EH-02's excavation/backfill/spoil transactions** must call `check_lot_provenance()` before `create_lot()` and `check_earth_withdrawal()` before a withdrawal. **The embedded-ledger columns are unbuilt and are EH-02's** — the arithmetic predicate is implemented; no capacity, default balance or column was invented.
3. A **stale checklist bullet** in task 02 still calls `excavated_earth` blocked, though the row is present at `count: 61`. It belongs to another lane, so it was reported rather than edited.
4. `economy_system.gd:515`'s `!= UNSET_PROVENANCE` is **still correct** under the new semantics (it now means "not ORDINARY"), but its header comment claiming the provenance catalog is unimplemented is now false.

ADR **0113**, deliberately leaving 0111 and 0112 free — 0111 turned out to be Astra's own record, which this PR's parent commits.

**No release-save completeness, no §15 certification, no MOVE gate.** The catalog identity moved deliberately; every save on the old digest refuses until an explicit versioned migration exists, and `1..5` is never reinterpreted blindly.

**`ok: 3765 tests, 132938 assertions, 0 failures.`** All four validators PASS — `state_registry_coverage` at 47 modules / 326 rows / 648 packed columns, `validate_underground_economy_hazards` 21/21.

## The problem in `gear.gd`

It had exactly **one** general-wear call, and it **releases the claim**. That is right for a fishing cycle and impossible for a construction phase worked by four builders across hundreds of ticks — the tool would come back after the first durability point.

Now three forms over one `_general_wear()`: `preflight_general_wear_into()` (writes nothing), `accrue_general_wear_into()` (debits, **keeps** the claim), `apply_general_wear_into()` (debits, releases — behaviour unchanged).

`work.gd` owns the settlement: a per-resident binding of `(tool lot ref, claiming job ref, broken byte)` taken once by `claim_tool_for_work()`. `_settle_wear()` charges `_party_share[index]` to the tool bound to `_party_resident[index]` — **the index is the attribution**, which is why there is one mutation per path rather than a single "wear works" test.

The binding exists for a stated performance reason: `gear.gd` resolves a lot ref by a bounded row scan and says gear ops are "never inside a per-tick loop", so the per-tick gate reads three packed columns and `gear.gd` is consulted only on the ~1-in-70 ticks a durability point falls due.

## The ledger entry is a move, not an addition

The agent found that `wear_remainder` is **already budgeted** in `systems_architecture.md` §3, inside ResidentRuntime's `I64 × 6 × 512 = 24576` group — for a store that **does not exist**. It implements the same field in `work.gd` at `I32 × 512`.

It flagged the choice and declined to make it. This PR takes the non-double-counting option: **4096 leaves that group, 10752 arrives, net +6656.** Budgeting one field in two places at two widths is exactly how a ledger drifts, and the row says so, as does the validator term.

Payload **63754547 → 63761203**, live → **72149811**, peak → **129695430**. **Verified row by row across all 30 trail rows.**

## Mutations: 11 plus a control, all resolved

A comment-only control mutant survived as expected — a harness sanity check I want to see more of.

**M11 exposed a real gap rather than confirming one.** Flipping `accrue_general_wear_into`'s release flag died **only in `test_gear.gd`**, because no work-level test ran past a single durability point — so a settlement that silently handed the gear back would have gone unnoticed there. A 375-tick, three-point test was added and M11 re-run: **4 failures, now including the work level.**

Also killed: `ceil` → `floor` in the tip rounding; charging the wrong contributor's tool; charging the wrong contributor's share; the settlement loop truncated to one party member; a refusal that still mutates; the broken-tool and stale-claim gates; the carry dropped; the threshold off by one.

## Generation namespaces, handled explicitly

`gear.gd`'s rows stay **bare indices and never escape it**. `work.gd` stores `InventoryLot` refs and Job refs — both generation-carrying — and compares the full `(slot, generation)` pair in both cases. All binding values are `Vector2i` components, which are int32-native, so no int64→int32 truncation path exists.

## One blocker, pinned rather than left to be discovered

**`jobs.tool_gate_into()` is needed and is not this lane's file.** `jobs.tool_gate_of()` allocates an `IntResult` per call, so the productive tick cannot read §5.3's tool gate without breaking the no-allocation rule.

The consequence is documented in `work.gd`'s header **and pinned by a test**: a tool-required job whose worker holds *no* binding produces work and wears nothing. Everything about a binding that *does* exist is enforced. The exact need: `func tool_gate_into(job_slot: int, out: IntMath.IntResult) -> bool` on `jobs.gd`.

## Not claimed

The fixed excavation costs (brace 2000, cut 4000, …) are EH-02's, along with the site phase domain, work-ready/commit-pending retry and `SPOIL_OUTPUT_BLOCKED`. `work.gd`'s only contribution to ECON-003's retry rule is that a further productive tick against a COMPLETE job is refused outright, which is tested. No performance budget is claimed as met — the per-tick cost argument is structural, not profiled. **No MOVE gate, no task 05.1b.**

ADR **0110**, taken deliberately above 0108/0109 to leave those clear for the two lanes allocating concurrently.

EH-04 reported the `InjuryKind` migration as a **blocker** and transcribed GDD §4.3 line 215 verbatim rather than working around it, because adding a protected domain moves the compiled-catalog digest and belongs to the catalog owner. EH-01 then published `InjuryKind` into `PROTECTED_ENUM_DOMAINS`.

Reconciled here: the six constants now **derive from `Catalog.INJURY_KIND`**. Two copies of a save-carried enum is exactly the drift decision 0018 exists to prevent.

`test_injury.gd` still asserts each number **literally**, deliberately — deriving them removes the chance of divergence, and the literal assertions are what make a renumbering of the *source* fail a test here rather than quietly re-labelling every saved injury in a world that already exists.

## Design decisions worth reading

**Death is final by ordering, not by a check.** `complete_treatment()` calls `apply_health_event(+10)` **before** it clears the injury, and that call refuses `RESIDENT_DEAD` before writing — so the clear is never reached. There is no post-hoc liveness re-check that a future edit could reorder past.

**No `_injury_severity` column was added.** `needs.gd`'s existing three-member `INJURY_*` input already distinguishes exactly the two authored rates: severity 1 → `INJURY_ACTIVE` (−1/hr), severity 2 → `INJURY_UNTREATED_SERIOUS` (−4/hr, and bars REQ-SET-017 recovery). Adding a column would have duplicated a distinction the domain already carries.

Every run restored and `shasum -a 256` byte-compared. body:
**`ok: 3700 tests, 126438 assertions, 0 failures.`** All five validators PASS, including `validate_underground_economy_hazards` at 21/21. Artifact check: `bytes=4161 sha256=d5bf21b4… domains=29 rows=282`.

## InjuryKind is protected, not compiled — and the reason is sharp

HAZ-001 requires the existing GDD §4.3 domain be reused. It is published verbatim as `NONE=0, CUT=1, BITE=2, FALL=3, EXPOSURE=4, EXHAUSTION=5`, plus `INJURY_KIND_DOMAIN` so the injury/care owner reads it rather than mirroring it.

It belongs in `PROTECTED_ENUM_DOMAINS` because ascending ASCII over its own keys generates `BITE=0, CUT=1, EXHAUSTION=2, EXPOSURE=3, FALL=4, NONE=5` — which **agrees on `CUT=1` and disagrees on the other five**. A partial coincidence is the dangerous shape: a silent regeneration would look half-right while landing `NONE`, the absence of injury, on `EXHAUSTION`'s number.

## The earth item: why the agent stopped, and what finished it

`excavated_earth` was fully authored by ECON-002 — the agent was not missing a number. It stopped on the **single-source rule**: `docs/gameplay_balance.md` §3.1 is the item catalog's one authored source, `tools/extract_item_definitions.py` extracts it mechanically, and `test_item_definitions.gd` runs that **real extractor as a subprocess against that real document**. Writing the key into the JSON or into `catalog.gd` would have created the hand-copied second catalog the pipeline exists to prevent, and the suite would have failed honestly when it did.

Completed here as integration lead, with values transcribed from the authored JSON and checked against it rather than retyped: `MATERIAL, 1000 g/U, nutrition 0, shelf 0, raw_edible 0, seed 0, NONE, 0`. `compost` is already `MATERIAL/1000` — **identical numbers** — which is exactly why a rename would have looked plausible and must not happen.

## An id shift worth understanding

**`ok: 3691 tests, 126345 assertions, 0 failures.`** `ready07_arithmetic` PASS, `state_registry_coverage` PASS (46 modules, 319 rows, 630 packed columns), `decision_numbers` PASS. **25 tests added, 2 rewritten, 0 deleted or weakened.**

Closes blocker D1: §3 could encode but could not capture or apply, because `entity_directory.gd`'s public surface answers only for *live* slots — so the generation of an **inactive** slot, the exact value the registry requires to survive verbatim, was unreachable.

## What landed

`copy_columns_into(...)` and `restore_columns(...)` as specified, plus two additions argued in the ADR:

- **`last_column_refusal()`** — a namespace separate from `create()`'s `last_refusal()`, every code prefixed `COLUMN_`. Sharing one field would let a save or a load clobber a `create()` refusal the caller had not read yet.
- **`state_bytes()`** — needed to assert the byte-identical rollback property rather than eyeballing it.

`restore_columns()` validates everything checkable **without mutation** first. The collision scan is the one step that must write, and on refusal `_typed_owner_slot` and `_kind_live_count` are rebuilt from the directory's own untouched columns by the same `_fill_owner_map()` — **exact**, because the reverse map is a pure function of `_active`/`_kind`/`_typed_row`.

## One judgement worth a second opinion

**`state_bytes()` emits each free window's live prefix *sorted*.** Raw would have been unusable: a live directory's heap is whatever permutation its pops left, a restored one is ascending, so two images of the same world would never compare equal. Decision 0103's own argument — that allocation order depends on the free *set*, not the permutation — says the permutation is not state.

It is mutation-proved non-vacuous: `state_bytes()` returning empty is killed by three assertions that require two images to **differ**.

## Mutations: 16 run, 16 killed

One per Godot invocation, each file `shasum -a 256` byte-compared after restore, failure counts parsed as integers. Both ascending-fill mutants die (descending free-slot fill kills 4 tests; descending free-row fill produces `expected 3, got 511`), as do live slots left in the free heap, a retired slot restored reusable, a duplicate `(kind,row)`, install-before-validate, each counter left unrebuilt, and the per-slot retirement check dropped — that last one caught by the **balanced swap** fixture decision 0103 introduced.

M1, M4 and M5 were re-run against the *committed* bytes and still die; the only post-mutation edit was a docstring line wrap.

## A finding worth keeping

**The round trip's "re-encodes byte for byte" assertion is vacuous against a `capture_into()` that publishes nothing** — both sides encode an empty world and agree. Only the allocation-order comparison caught that mutant. A non-vacuousness assertion on the captured record was added afterwards.

That generalises: a symmetric round-trip test can pass on two empty halves, so at least one assertion has to be about *content* rather than agreement.

## Blocker D2 is now more visible, and deliberately untouched

A world can be reloaded with every slot, generation and retirement intact **and still reissue persistent IDs from 1**, because §1 WORLD carries no `next_persistent_id` and `restore_columns()` deliberately does not write it.

Two tests state that in the positive rather than leaving it implicit: `test_restore_columns_does_not_restore_the_persistent_id_allocator` asserts the restored image **differs** from the saved one, sets that one scalar by hand, then asserts the images are identical — **so it fails if anyone starts restoring it here, and also fails if the rebuild stops being exact**.

Closing D2 needs `save_section_world_runtime.gd`'s block to carry the field and the directory to expose a reader. Both are outside this task's allowlist, and the wire half is blocked on the canonical owner/field registry that the save-registry request covers.

## Registry rows applied here

The column-refusal namespace as a category-3 row — a `StringName` scalar, not a packed column, so **no allocation row and no ledger byte**. The heaps row now also records that ascending refill is `restore_columns()`'s obligation, not only `_rebuild_free_heaps()`'s, since that is the property the round trip actually tests.

All four validators PASS. Documents only.

Astra reviewed the MOVE-G01 request and found **four material overstatements**. Each was checked against the code before being accepted — all four hold. The request's original text is **preserved unedited**, per the review's own handoff instruction; corrections are appended below it so a reader sees both the claim and what was wrong with it.

## C1 — the one worth remembering

The request framed clearance as absent. **The domain already exists.** `spatial_world.gd` declares classes over a 512×512 grid of `CELL_SIZE_UNITS = 512` half-metre cells, where `_clearance[cell]` is *"the side of the largest all-passable square whose north-west corner is that cell"* — anchored, not centred, with `CELL_CENTRE_OFFSET_UNITS = 256`.

**That file's own header says so**, including that it publishes no body or gear clearance number *because exact production clearances are a profile decision*. The request should have asked the narrower question it actually meant.

What is genuinely missing is each profile's **body/gear envelope** and **proof of placement within the anchored square**. `ceil(max(width, depth)/512)` bounds the size and does not prove placement, and the 256u centre offset cannot be treated as the centre of a larger square. The refusal is not softened: `PROFILE_CLEARANCE_UNSPECIFIED` stays, and a guessed body width must not turn it into an apparent pass.

## C2–C4

**C2.** `needs.apply_health_event()` and `set_injury_state()` already exist; GDD §5.4/5.5 assign fishing and foraging health loss and severity, REQ-SET-172 sets untreated damage at ¼ health/hour, REQ-SET-173 owns treatment. The request conflated absence of settlement *combat* with absence of health *loss*. Still owed: the aggregate Injury store, hazard integration and the hazard rules.

**C3.** REQ-SET-124–128 and 137 already rule delivery, consumption, 100%/80% refund and demolition. Underground excavation and spoil are **extensions to that owner**, not a second building or inventory system.

**C4.** Q1+Q2 do not unblock swimming or climbing — speeds, durations, equipment, posture, supported exits and **Q5 interruption** apply on the surface too. Full 05.1b needs **G02's bindings after G01**; the task text never said otherwise.

## Two more corrections

**Mode states are three, not two.** `UNPROFILED` (missing data or implementation — *may not masquerade as an animal's inherent inability*), `DISABLED` (authored restriction, with a reason and what could change it), `ENABLED`. The request asked for two. No species-mode permission table is approved, and no universal "moles cannot swim" may be inferred.

**CHILD/ELDER immobility is explicitly not an approved release design.** DEC-032 requires visible dependent residents and active elders; `LIFE_STAGE_NOT_PROFILED` is temporary pending PC-04 and must not be removed by substituting adult coefficients. Four adults-only profiles are a legitimate starter increment but not the release catalog — all 16 admitted species need profiles, and **a badger height approval does not make a badger profile**.

## Three proposals now on the table, awaiting Brendan

Recorded as candidates, explicitly not constants, and none will be implemented until answered: **four underground levels at 4 m spacing** (−4096/−8192/−12288/−16384 u; implying 65536 tile addresses, and 14680064 bytes if naively arrayed); **real haulable, reusable spoil** with its own catalog key and mass, not stone or compost renamed; and **warned, preventable hazards with rescue** rather than surprise death rolls.

## DEC-039, and the structural cause of the miss

The review could not locate DEC-039 and correctly recorded it as *"executor-reported, source not located"* rather than disproven. **It is on master**, in `docs/setting_decisions.md`, with `SPECIES_HEIGHT_U` reading `[1024, 922, 1178, 1526, 2611]` and every status approved. Heights are not reverting.

The cause is structural, not clerical: **`DEC-nnn` records live in `setting_decisions.md` while `NNNN` records live in `docs/decisions/`, and nothing said so.** An auditor searching the decision log for a *user* decision comes up empty every time. `docs/decisions/README.md` now states the split and cites this miss as the reason it exists.

MOVE-G01 remains **OPEN**. Nothing here closes a gate.

A request document, not a ruling. It proposes no value.

**05.1b — the first playable connected movement — is the only unchecked item in task 05, and it is blocked on this gate alone.**

It takes the amendment's five closure terms one at a time, states what `movement.gd` refuses to invent and why each refusal is correct, and says what shape an answer has to take to be usable.

## What it deliberately does not re-ask

The starter ground profile is built, not stubbed, and `_build_starter_profiles()` derives every number from `residents.gd` — refusing a species the store cannot compile rather than letting it inherit a neighbour's numbers. Speed (3277/4096/3072 u·s⁻¹), carry (12000/16000/24000 g), the four compiled profiles and DEC-039's approved heights are all recorded as **already authored**, with a note that GDD §5.2's large-is-slower anomaly is deliberate and is not a defect report.

## The five questions

1. **Clearance class** — `profile_clearance_class_into()` refuses for *every* profile today. The trap is stated plainly: **height is not a cross-section.** A mole is the shortest of the five and the widest through the shoulder; a squirrel is taller than a mouse and slighter than an otter. The landmark ratios are still `PROPOSED_FOR_REVIEW` and are explicitly not a clearance authority.
2. **The four unprofiled modes** — six are enumerated so scope cannot narrow by omission; `PROFILED_MODE_MASK` admits two. The request asks for allowed *and* disabled cases separately, because **they are not complements**: a mode nobody has specified and a mode a mole is forbidden from must refuse differently, or the UI cannot tell a player "not built yet" from "moles do not swim".
3. **Depth extents** — nothing is authored. The building envelopes are above-datum maxima and the asset ruling says in terms that they do not set underground depth or clearance, so there is nothing to extrapolate from.
4. **Construction states, costs and spoil rules** — with the spoil rule called out as the one most likely to be skipped and the one that changes the economy: if spoil is a real item, every excavation generates hauling and consumes container capacity; if it evaporates, digging is nearly free.
5. **Interruption and hazard policy** — noting that `Injury` is modelled with healing and **no damage model** in the settlement layer, so drowning or cave-in must either be expressed in existing terms or the ruling must say a new one is being added.

## Two smaller items in the same area

**Profile coverage** — four species are profiled; DEC-039 approved a badger height and the admitted species list is longer. Does 05.1b need all of them?

**Life stage** — decision 0095 landed the fixed ADULT/CHILD/ELDER column and decision 0101 made admission read it, but **only ADULT is profiled**, so a CHILD or ELDER resident is refused travel outright. If that is right for release 1 the ruling should say so. No adult-coefficient fallback will be invented, per MOVE-DEP-R02.

## Scope

Q1 and Q2 alone unblock surface work for 05.1b; Q3–Q5 are required for underground and for MOVE-TEST-01. Nothing here closes G02–G05, and no answer authorizes paid generation.

Supersedes PR #63, whose CONFLICTING flag was stale — this branch merges master cleanly.

## What happened

Decision 0002's required comparison **already existed and was already rendered**. It was sitting unmerged on a stale branch, which is why this read for weeks as "waiting on Brendan" when it was actually waiting on someone to put it in front of him.

Shown the elevation, he asked for exactly one change before approving: **the squirrel was to be taller than the mouse.** They were identical at 1024 u — the only pair in the set with no separation.

| Species | u (1/1024 m) | mm | vs mouse | Tail ‰ | Crown set by |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| mouse | 1024 | 1000 | 1.00× | 820 | ears |
| mole | 922 | 900 | 0.90× | 120 | skull |
| **squirrel** | **1178** | **1150** | **1.15×** | **950** | ears |
| otter | 1526 | 1490 | 1.49× | 620 | skull |
| badger | 2611 | 2550 | 2.55× | 250 | skull |

**Why 1.15× and not more:** the whole set is compressed — the badger is only 2.55× the mouse — so a taller squirrel crowds the otter at 1.49× and loses the distinction between a lithe silhouette and a genuinely bigger animal. The squirrel's tail is already 950‰ of its height, the longest in the set, and its ears set its crown; the extra height compounds the leggiest silhouette rather than fighting it.

## What this approval is, and is not

The heights are now production values and every status says so. **Two things deliberately do not move with them:**

- **The mouse keeps `ANCHOR_SOURCED`**, because its 1.0 m came from crowd §9.1, not from this review. Flattening that to a plain "approved" would lose the provenance distinction.
- **`LANDMARK_STATUS` stays `PROPOSED_FOR_REVIEW`.** DEC-039 ruled on scale *between* species; where the eye, hip and shoulder sit *within* a body is a different question and was not what this review judged.

It is **not** paid-generation authorization — the asset generation lock governs that separately — and the proxies deliberately carry no fur, face or costume, because texture would have obscured the scale relationships the review exists to settle.

## Two tests inverted, both recording why they were right before

`test_every_species_row_is_labelled_as_a_comparison_input` required every status to contain `COMPARISON`, and `test_the_landmarks_are_labelled_as_review_inputs` required the height status to contain `NOT_PRODUCTION_APPROVAL`. Both were correct until DEC-039 and now pin the defect.

Each is rewritten to assert the approved state **positively** — `contains("APPROVED")` rather than the absence of a denial — while still pinning what remains unapproved: the anchor's provenance, and the landmarks. The old assertions are quoted in the new docstrings.

`--headless` cannot capture at all: Godot's dummy renderer returns null from `ViewportTexture.get_image()`, exactly as the build script's own header warns, and a headless run refuses all six views by name rather than writing empty files. This went through a real windowed render on the M5 Pro, and the manifest carries fresh SHA-256s for all six.

**A2 mole, A3 squirrel, A4 otter.** GAP-01 closes; GAP-02's height half closes, with battle horizontal radii still explicitly a separate measurement from which no production ratio is inferred.

**`ok: 3538 tests, 124880 assertions, 0 failures.`** after merging current master. `ready07_arithmetic` PASS (27 allocation rows), `state_registry_coverage` PASS, `decision_numbers` PASS. `game_manager.gd` was read-only and never edited.

This closes the hole decision 0092 shipped with and named: `clock()` and `scheduler_events()` hand out the real objects, whose own mutators knew nothing about the barrier.

## The design question, answered

**Where the state lives: in a token, not a flag.** `acquire_load_barrier()` returns a grant; the token's private `_held` bool *is* the barrier. The clock holds a reference and reads it; **it exposes no call that lowers it.**

**What stops an arbitrary caller lowering it:** there is no public lowering API on either object — no setter, no flag, no callback registration, no rebind that escapes it. The only route down is `release()` on the exact object the loader was handed. A second concurrent acquire refuses with `CLOCK_LOAD_BARRIER_ALREADY_HELD` and **mints no token**; a spent token has no authority over a later load. Dropping the token without releasing leaves the barrier **up** — the safe failure direction.

The ADR is explicit about the limit rather than overclaiming: GDScript has no access control, so `clock.get("_load_barrier")` still reaches the token by reflection, and no GDScript construct closes that.

**Layering:** `scheduler_events.gd` preloads `sim_clock.gd`; `game_manager.gd` preloads both; nothing in `scripts/core/` may preload `scripts/systems/`. So the barrier lives at the bottom, on the clock, and **the queue reads it through its bound clock rather than carrying a second one** — one barrier per world, no circular dependency, and unit fixtures stay free of the autoload. A public flag with a declared writer was rejected as exactly the convention 0092 already found insufficient one layer up; an owner-registered callback was rejected because state moves back to the registrant, stale registrations outlive the loader, and it adds indirection on the per-frame `advance()` path.

**Does `restore_runtime()` pass through?** It ignores the barrier **structurally**: the guard is `_command_barred()` and only *command* entry points call it — RESTORE-R01 says "Restore is not such a command". To stop that being incidental via shared code, `restore_extension()` and `_init()` now reset through a private `_reset_to_initial_state()` instead of the public `clear()` they used to call, **so barring the command cannot break the install.**

Also enforced: a barred call mutates **nothing** — not `_last_error`, `_last_diagnostic`, `_last_refusal` or `_refused_count` — though a caller-owned `SubmitResult` *is* filled, because that is output, not state. The barrier never touches the pause mask, and lowering it never clears a *saved* `LOAD` bit. No sentinel returns: `apply_overload`, `apply_overload_target`, `note_overload_step`, `begin_host_frame` and `clear` changed `void` → `bool` so refusal is explicit.

## Mutations: 27, all died

One per Godot invocation, restored and `shasum -a 256` byte-compared, 600 s `perl -e 'alarm'` timeouts. **One mutation per guarded mutator** — seven on the clock, ten on the queue — because a single "the barrier works" test proves one call site. Plus the four that matter most: `restore_runtime` blocked by the barrier it serves; the barrier ORing LOAD into the pause mask (8 failures); the barrier clearing a *saved* LOAD bit; a guard that refuses but still writes `_last_error`.

**Two survived on the first pass and the tests were fixed, not the mutants.** `rebind_clock`'s test left an event queued, so `SCHEDULER_QUEUE_NOT_EMPTY` refused it with or without the barrier — replaced with a test on an **empty** queue that would otherwise rebind freely. `advance_frame`'s own guard was unobservable because its inner `pump_into` and `_clock.advance()` are both barred anyway — the test now spends the frame's single overload issue first and asserts it is still spent, which only holds if the frame was **never opened**. Both then died, and the neighbouring mutants were re-run to confirm the edits had not weakened them.

## Ledger: +9 bytes, applied and verified

An 8-byte object reference plus the 1-byte RefCounted token it points at, **counted at its maximum of one** because a second concurrent acquire refuses and mints none. `scheduler_events.gd` adds no field; its 8224-byte row is unchanged, and **no packed column is added**, so the persistence registry is owed nothing.

Identities advance to payload **63733043**, live **72121651**, headroom **27878349**, candidate **57517459**, peak **129639110**, transactional headroom **−29639110**. Allocation rows 25 → 27. **Verified row by row across all 28 trail rows**, not by comparing totals.

## Still open, and stated plainly

**`game_manager.gd` does not raise this barrier yet, so the hole is still open in the running game.** The mechanism exists and is tested; the wiring is three lines in a file this lane did not own — take the grant beside the existing checkpoint capture and refuse the whole `begin_load()` if acquisition refuses (preserving its "nothing changed" contract); release in `end_load()` and `rollback_load()` where each already resets `_last_host_usec`; one transient reference field. `GameManager._loading` should **stay** — it guards the coordinator's own controls and `_process`; they are one barrier's two checkpoints. I'll wire it separately.

**Task 09.3 is not complete and is not claimed.** This closes one named half of RESTORE-R01. The disk-backed checkpoint, file rotation and I/O fault injection belong to another owner.

Reviewer note: `SchedulerEvents.clear()` and the three ladder entry points changed `void` → `bool`. Existing call sites that discard the result still compile; `game_manager.gd:278` is unaffected.

ADR renumbered **0098 → 0104**, with all three citations moved — both production file headers and the task-09 subsection.

**Written (category 1), six columns and nothing else**: `_active` u8, `_generation` i32, `_retired` u8, `_persistent_id` i32, `_kind` i32, `_typed_row` i32 — SAVE-LAYOUT-R01's stated order, full capacity, column-major.

**Rebuilt, never written (category 2)**: `_typed_owner_slot`, both heaps, the three per-kind counters and the two totals. The reason is sharper than "derived": `_pop_min()` returns the **window minimum**, so allocation order depends on the free *set*, not on the permutation — which is also why the tail beyond `_free_count` is stale garbage. **Two observationally identical worlds hold different garbage there**, so writing the heaps would produce different bytes and different CRCs for the same world. `rebuild_into()` is simultaneously the validator: a duplicate `(kind, row)` is caught precisely because two live slots try to own one arena entry.

**Digest membership**, stated as a finding rather than assumed: all six written columns are hashed per ARCH-HASH-001; every category-2 member is excluded from **both** saving and hashing. §3 has **no** saved-but-not-hashed field, unlike §1's host debt and clock counters — a real difference between the sections, not an oversight.

## Chunking was required, so it was built

ARCH-SAVE-003 mandates 65536-byte chunks for large sections, and at 6.3 MB this qualifies. `ChunkCursor` emits ≤65536 bytes per chunk, **field-aligned** so no chunk straddles two columns: 107 chunks, largest 65536, 625 µs to drain. It deliberately does **not** fold CRC itself — `save_header.gd::crc32_update()` is already the incremental register API, and the caller must fold the body SHA-256 over the same bytes anyway.

Round trip: encode 12374 µs → decode 10545 µs, `equals=true`, **re-encode byte-identical=true**, 6343616 bytes both times. Real byte vectors for a four-slot fixture are in the PR's source ADR, including the never-used slot 100000 pinned at `active=0 gen=0 retired=0 pid=0 kind=-1 row=-1`.

## Mutations: 11 killed, and one of them found a real hole

One per Godot invocation, restored and `shasum -a 256` byte-compared; `restored_byte_identical` on all 12 runs.

**M4 — dropping the per-retired-slot generation check — survived at first**, because a whole-column retirement *count* subsumed it for every case tested. It does not subsume a **balanced swap**: slot 4 retired at generation 10 while slot 5 holds the spent generation un-retired. The counts cancel; only the per-slot check sees it; and a loader trusting the count would hand slot 4 back to the allocator **and never reuse slot 5**. `test_a_retirement_swap_that_keeps_the_counts_balanced_is_still_refused` closes it and M4 dies.

A second gap found the same way: M2 (never-used generation `fill(0)` → `fill(1)`) survived until `test_a_never_used_slot_holds_its_declared_canonical_values` pinned slot 100000's six values **on the wire**. Commit-then-validate was tested against a **full-length** invalid section (a live slot's kind patched to 18), not truncation.

## Two blockers, neither invented around

**D1 — `entity_directory.gd` has no bulk column reader or writer.** Its public surface answers only for *live* slots, so the generation of an **inactive** slot — the exact value the registry says must survive verbatim — is unreachable. No module in this repo reads another's underscore columns and this one did not become the first; the precedent is `save_section_world_runtime.gd`'s blocker W1, which was later ruled into `restore_runtime()`.

So there is **no `apply()`**: `capture_columns_into(...)` takes the six columns, and `capture_into(store, out)` refuses with `SAVE_DIR_STORE_NO_COLUMN_READER` **and names the API it needs** — `copy_columns_into(...)` and `restore_columns(...)`, with the note that `restore_columns()` must rebuild the owner map, both heaps and all five counters, filling every window **ascending**, because ascending fill is what makes the next `create()` return the lowest free slot.

**D2 — `_next_persistent_id` is registered to §1 WORLD and nobody writes it.** Not derivable: `destroy()` zeroes `_persistent_id`, so "max live id + 1" is wrong after any death. §1's 80-byte block does not carry it and the directory exposes no reader. **Until both owners act, a reloaded world reissues persistent IDs and fails ARCH-SAVE-004.** §3 deliberately does not write it — that would duplicate one future-affecting value across two sections.

## Open by external dependency, labelled as such

`owner_key` is `"entity_directory"`, read off SAVE-LAYOUT-R01's own "exactly one entity_directory block"; no formal owner-key registry is published. SAVE-R09's canonical `field_key` registry is **not frozen**, so `ColumnCursor` emits canonical **values only** and leaves the `section_id/owner_key/field_key/type/value_count` prefix to §15; `FIELD_KEYS` and `canonical_type_of()` ship as a labelled proposal, not a fait accompli.

ADR renumbered **0098 → 0103**: 0098 was taken twice concurrently, by the resident identity row (merged first) and the clock load barrier. The registry row is the agent's own text, applied here because that file was outside its allowlist; its patch conflicted with §14's section landing at the same anchor and both are kept.

**`ok: 3536 tests, 124738 assertions, 0 failures.`** after merging current master. `ready07_arithmetic` and `state_registry_coverage` PASS. `stock_age.gd` and `test_stock_age.gd` are **byte-identical to master**; no existing test was weakened or deleted.

The gap was confirmed first, not assumed: in a fresh worktree, `refuses_seed_consumption` appeared only in its own definition, its own test, ADR 0093 and a checklist — **no production caller**.

## The design, and the judgement the ruling forced

Inventory knows an item's mass and category only — **it cannot tell a seed from a stone** — and `stock_age.gd` already preloads `inventory.gd`, so the dependency cannot be circular. Enforcement therefore delegates through a duck-typed **seed-expiry authority**, the same shape already used for the equipment authority. No shelf-life arithmetic and no seed flag is duplicated.

Seven guarded paths, each asking in **its own** precondition check rather than one shared choke point — deliberately, so each is independently mutation-killable: `reserve_lot`, `sink_lot_quantity`, `consume_reserved`, `transfer`, `move_lot`, `split_lot`, `transform_lot_item`.

**Commit-time revalidation is structural:** there is no verdict cache anywhere, so an earlier "yes" has nowhere to be stored and cannot be replayed.

### The exemption problem, and why it isn't a hole

Cleanup and consumption reach the store through *the same two methods*: `stock_age.gd`'s zero-yield retirement calls `sink_lot_quantity()` — the same call `economy_system.gd:240` uses to take a helping — and its conversion calls `transform_lot_item()`. Guarding them naively would make the expiry sweep unable to dispose of the very lots it just condemned.

Since `stock_age.gd` was read-only, the exemption had to be recognisable from what it already does. `release_all_reservations()` now sets a **single-use cleanup declaration** that names one lot (inventory **lot** generation, never the container one), is taken-and-cleared by the next `_enter()`, is recorded before `_leave()` so an implicit transaction discards it, and **exempts nothing partial** — the sink must take the row's entire remaining quantity with no claim standing.

The consequence is the point: a consumer can only reach the exemption by cancelling every claim and destroying the whole lot in one transaction — the ruling's permitted combination, which hands the consumer nothing.

## Mutations: 17, all killed

One per Godot invocation, restored and `shasum -a 256` byte-compared each time. One mutation per guarded path, so a single "the guard works" test cannot stand in for seven. Also killed: commit-time revalidation removed; fail-open **only** for an authority that cannot evaluate; blunt fail-open (10 failures); a refusal mutating an unjournaled ledger cell before refusing (7); the exemption widened to a partial sink; the declaration losing single-use, crossing a transaction, or ceasing to name a lot.

**Two survivors were fixed rather than reported away**, and one of them was a real hole. The first draft had two lines enforcing one invariant — a redundant `and _tx_open` and an equivalent-mutant clear — so neither was individually load-bearing. Collapsing them exposed that without the `_op_cleanup_lot` clear, **a spent declaration licensed a second transform of the same row**. `test_a_spent_declaration_does_not_come_back_in_the_next_transaction` closes it; M13/M14 then died.

## One wiring line is owed, and until it lands this is enforced only in the suite

With no authority bound, nothing is refused — Inventory cannot identify a seed alone, and refusing every lot instead would halt the settlement. Enforcement goes live when `settlement_system.gd` calls:

```gdscript
inventory.set_seed_expiry_authority(stock_age)
```

**That file was outside this lane's allowlist and was not touched.** The limitation is stated in the ADR, the module header and the task checklist rather than left for someone to discover. I'll wire it separately.

## Ledger: nothing owed

No new packed column. The verdict derives from the existing `_l_age_milli_hours` column plus the item definition — the ruling says as much ("requires no new per-lot flag or remainder store"). The three new fields are a wiring reference and two transaction-scratch `Vector2i`s: not journaled, absent from `state_bytes()`, not saved.

One refactor inside the owned file: `_move_lot_checked()` was split to stay under 30 lines, with no behaviour change, verified by the unchanged move tests.
